Subject: Data residency + retention configuration Qs for upcoming POC

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — FinEdge is excited to move the POC forward. Before we start, our legal and security teams asked for a clear picture of how Redwood supports per-tenant data residency and configurable retention/deletion policies. A few concrete asks below: 

- Can we pin a tenant to EU-only storage (data at rest) and ensure no backups/replicas leave the region?
- Is retention configurable per-tenant and per-data-type (prompt logs, embeddings, cache TTL)?
- Do you provide deletion APIs that guarantee removal from KV caches, hot-storage, and cold backups within an SLA window?
- What audit evidence (logs, timestamps) would you provide for an attestation?

Attached is our short RFP excerpt that lists the minimal controls we need. We need answers by Dec 7 to finish our procurement packet. Appreciated if you can loop in product/eng owners.

Best,

Thanks Jordan — quick product take below. I also added where we can make a firm commitment for the POC vs what is roadmap work.

Summary (product vantage):
- EU-only storage: For Hosted we can offer region-scoped tenants that are pinned to the EU cluster; however, snapshot replication currently replicates to a DR location within the same jurisdiction group (EU regional replicas only). We cannot guarantee air-gapped backups without a Private deployment.
- Per-tenant retention: We support TTL flags on logs and embeddings at the application layer; present UI/API is account-level (not per-dataset). Per-tenant + per-data-type granularity is on the roadmap — estimate: Q2 2027 for incremental rollout (can accelerate to Q1 with dedicated engineering allocation).
- Deletion guarantees: We have deletion APIs that mark objects for immediate deletion and purge from primary stores quickly. KV cache entries live in memory; cache eviction is fast but not atomic with background persistence. Cold backups are on daily snapshots — purge from backups requires a separate workflow (we can offer documented attestations once purge completes). Target SLA for full purge across all layers today is ~30 days; with prioritized effort we can commit to 14 days for the POC if required.
- Audit evidence: We can provide deletion event logs, S3 lifecycle logs, and an exported timeline per-tenant. We can map these to common controls and provide a short attestation template.

Action items I recommend: 
1) Offer FinEdge a written POC commitment: EU-region pinning + 14-day purge SLA for tenant data (hosted), and list limitations (replica/backup constraints).
2) Karthik: can you validate the engineering feasibility and flag any blockers (esp. backup purge and KV cache invalidation guarantees)?
3) Laura: prepare a short attestation template and SOC2 control crosswalk sample.

Happy to run a short sync with FinEdge if they want to walk through the proposed commitment.

—Evelyn
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 14:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Data residency + retention configuration Qs for upcoming POC

Thanks — technical notes and risks below. TL;DR: EU pinning and per-tenant TTLs are feasible for Hosted with engineering work; backup purge/replica guarantees are the trickiest piece.

Technical feasibility checklist:
- Tenant EU pinning: straightforward at the routing and storage config layer. Need to ensure orchestration doesn't failover to non-EU DR during major outage — would require a policy toggle (keep within EU-only DR) and additional DR capacity in-region. Estimated 3 sprints to complete policy + tests.
- Per-data-type retention (prompt logs vs embeddings vs cache): we already tag data objects; adding per-tenant per-type TTLs is an extension of current lifecycle hooks. Estimate 6 sprints (backend + UI/CLI) for a minimal viable implementation.
- KV cache deletion: cache eviction is eventual. To guarantee deletion we need to propagate a deletion event to the serving tier and block reads for that tenant on sight — this adds complexity and may temporarily increase latency. Estimate 2 sprints to implement strong invalidation semantics for targeted tenants.
- Backup/snapshot purge: current backups are incremental daily snapshots and tape-style cold storage in a regional bucket. Removal from cold backups requires a retention rewrite process that re-writes snapshots without the deleted objects (expensive). For an SLA of <=14 days we'll need an indexing layer to speed targeted purges or maintain shorter snapshot retention for pinned tenants. This is non-trivial: estimate 8-10 sprints and possibly additional storage costs.

Risks/notes:
- Cost: per-tenant shorter snapshot retention and re-writes will increase storage and IO costs. We should surface cost estimates to the customer.
- Complexity: delivering strong deletion guarantees across all layers is a cross-cutting change touching serving, backup, and orchestration.

Recommendation: For the POC we can offer EU pinning + per-tenant TTL for active stores + a 14-day purge SLA with the caveat that cold-backup purge is best-effort and will be handled by a prioritized engineering stream (JIRA-INFRA-1428). For a hardened long-term SLA, recommend Dedicated or Private deployment which gives us more control over backup topology.

—Karthik
Engineering Director, Redwood Inference

Marta — thanks for the detailed ask and patience while we scoped this internally. Below is our proposed POC commitment and next steps; happy to jump on a call to walk through.

POC commitment (Hosted):
- Tenant-level EU region pinning for data-at-rest and runtime (we will not route tenant traffic outside EU clusters; DR stays within EU regional group).
- Per-tenant per-data-type TTLs for active stores (prompt logs, embeddings, session KV) with API + UI controls.
- Deletion API that begins immediate purge from primary stores and propagates an invalidation to serving caches. We commit to full purge across active stores and caches within 14 days.
- Cold-backup purge: we will attempt targeted purge and provide a documented attestation timeline; full removal from long-term backups may require additional engineering work. We will prioritize FinEdge as part of INFRA-1428.
- Evidence: deletion event logs, S3 lifecycle events, snapshot manifests, and an attestation template will be provided after purge completion.

Next steps:
1) Laura will send the attestation template and SOC2 control crosswalk by EOD Dec 8.
2) We will schedule a 30-minute sync with you and your privacy team on Dec 9 (propose 09:30 CET) to confirm wording of the POC commitment.
3) Karthik will open the JIRA ticket and share the technical plan and cost implications (JIRA-INFRA-1428).
4) Jordan will share the retention-options-matrix and the tenant config example for review (attached).

If that sounds good I’ll confirm the Dec 9 time. We attached the tenant-config-example.json with the suggested tenant flags.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
